items.title: NHKこどもパーク【公式】
items.creator: NHK / NHK Enterprises
items.why: Official clips of NHK E-tele children's programmes: simple, clear standard Japanese.
items.notes: Clear, slow speech for small children. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Also promotes paid Prime Video access for full shows. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: しまじろうチャンネル（YouTube）
items.creator: Benesse
items.why: Benesse's preschool tiger character: songs and short stories in very simple Japanese.
items.notes: Slow, clear speech. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: それいけ!アンパンマン【アニメ公式】
items.creator: TMS / Froebel-kan
items.why: Classic preschool anime with short, simple, kind dialogue.
items.notes: Official clips and songs. Slow speech. Sampled videos had no captions at all. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: ペッパピッグ Peppa Pig - 公式チャンネル
items.creator: Hasbro / Entertainment One
items.why: Japanese dub of Peppa Pig: everyday family situations in short sentences.
items.notes: Clear, slow narration. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: にほんごのじかん | Japanese Comprehensible Input (CI)
items.creator: Yuki
items.why: Relaxed CI videos in very simple Japanese with drawings, for absolute beginners up.
items.notes: Uploaded Japanese CC on every sampled video. Very slow speech. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: Natural Japanese (NIJ)
items.creator: Yuki Kimura and team
items.why: Large library of graded all-Japanese CI videos from complete beginner to advanced.
items.notes: Formerly the Comprehensible Japanese channel (@cijapanese). Spans all levels; beginner videos are level 1. Two of three sampled videos had uploaded Japanese CC. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: Teppei (Nihongo con Teppei)
items.creator: Teppei
items.why: Short podcast episodes in natural but easy Japanese about daily life.
items.notes: Mostly audio with a still image. Slow to moderate speed. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: けんさんおかえり Japanese
items.creator: Ken
items.why: Immersion content in easy, friendly Japanese for listening practice.
items.notes: Uploaded Japanese CC on every sampled video. Slow to moderate speed. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: Japanese with Shun
items.creator: Shun
items.why: Vlogs, interviews and travel in easy Japanese aimed at N5-N3 learners.
items.notes: Moderate speed. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Japanese subtitles are usually burned in. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: Onomappu
items.creator: Onomappu
items.why: Japanese onomatopoeia and daily-life videos explained mostly in Japanese.
items.notes: Uploaded Japanese and English CC on sampled videos. Moderate speed. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: Kurashiru
items.creator: dely (Kurashiru app)
items.why: Short recipe videos with simple on-screen instructions in Japanese.
items.notes: Mostly text and music, little speech. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Steps are burned in. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: Koh Kentetsu Kitchen【料理研究家コウケンテツ公式チャンネル】
items.creator: コウケンテツ (Koh Kentetsu)
items.why: A cook talking warmly and calmly while making everyday Japanese meals.
items.notes: Relaxed speed, some Kansai flavour. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Captions often burned in. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: Nami's life
items.creator: Nami
items.why: Quiet vlog of living alone in Tokyo with short written narration.
items.notes: Little speech; uploaded CC in Japanese and dozens of languages on every sampled video. Better as reading practice. Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: はじめしゃちょー（hajime）
items.creator: はじめしゃちょー
items.why: One of Japan's biggest YouTubers: experiments and challenges in fast casual Japanese.
items.notes: Fast, casual speech with burned-in captions. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: 東海オンエア
items.creator: 東海オンエア
items.why: Six-man comedy group doing challenges; very fast group banter and slang.
items.notes: Fast, overlapping speech with burned-in captions. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: ゆる言語学ラジオ
items.creator: 水野太貴, 堀元見
items.why: Two hosts chat about language and linguistics; fast, intellectual Japanese.
items.notes: Fast talk, academic vocabulary. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: ANNnewsCH
items.creator: TV Asahi
items.why: TV Asahi network news: formal newsreader Japanese.
items.notes: Formal news register; on-screen telops. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: 日テレNEWS
items.creator: Nippon TV
items.why: Nippon TV news reports and live streams in formal Japanese.
items.notes: Formal news register; on-screen telops. Sampled videos had no uploaded Japanese CC (auto-generated only). Channel ID read from the channel page on 2026-11-06.

items.title: 日本の絵本 (Storybooks Japan)
items.creator: Global Storybooks / African Storybook (translations)
items.why: 40 short illustrated stories tagged レベル1-5, one or two short sentences per page, with audio narration.
items.notes: Enumerate: the index page lists every story card with its level; story pages follow /storybooks-japan/stories/ja/NNNN/ (4-digit ID) and contain the text as plain HTML (checked: 0087 本を読むのが好き！). Level split about 15/11/8/4/2 for levels 1-5. Same IDs exist in the Spanish and French sites.

items.title: StoryWeaver（日本語の絵本）
items.creator: Pratham Books
items.why: About 1,000 free picture books in Japanese with publisher reading levels 1-4; level 1 has a few words per page.
items.notes: Enumerate with the public JSON search API: https://storyweaver.org.in/api/v1/books-search?languages[]=Japanese&levels[]=1&per_page=24&page=N (returns title, slug, level). Counts on 2026-11-06: L1 552, L2 341, L3 89, L4 22. Metadata from /api/v1/stories/{slug}. The reader is a JS app and /api/v1/stories/{slug}/read returned 401 without a session, so the browser must render the reader page before scoring. Stories are CC BY 4.0 but many are translations from English or Hindi.

items.title: にほんごたどく 無料で読める本
items.titleEn: NPO Tadoku Supporters free graded readers
items.creator: NPO多言語多読 (NPO Tadoku Supporters)
items.why: Free graded readers from Level Start/0 (a few words per page with pictures) up to level 5, written for adult learners.
items.notes: Enumerate by level with https://tadoku.org/japanese/book-search?level=l0 (also l-start, l1, l2...); book pages are /japanese/book/{id}/. Books come as an image page-flipper, PDF and YouTube video, not HTML text, so the extension cannot score them as text. Licence is Creative Commons; the book page checked said CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

items.title: キツネとツル～イソップ物語より
items.titleEn: The Fox and the Crane (from Aesop)
items.creator: NPO多言語多読; illustrated by 高橋智子
items.why: Tadoku Level 0: 12 illustrated pages, one short sentence each, a familiar Aesop plot.
items.notes: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Text is inside images/PDF, not HTML.

items.title: 金の斧銀の斧～イソップ物語より
items.titleEn: The Golden Axe and the Silver Axe (from Aesop)
items.creator: NPO多言語多読
items.why: Tadoku Level 1 retelling of a well-known fable: short sentences, basic polite forms, pictures on every page.
items.notes: Free online reader and PDF on the book page.

items.title: おいしいおかゆ
items.creator: NPO多言語多読
items.why: Tadoku Level 2: a longer folk tale with simple past-tense narration and pictures.
items.notes: Free online reader and PDF on the book page.

items.title: NEWS WEB EASY（やさしいことばニュース）
items.creator: NHK
items.why: Daily news rewritten in short sentences with furigana and audio; learners usually start it around N4-N3.
items.notes: Changed in 2025-26: www3.nhk.or.jp/news/easy/ now redirects to news.web.nhk/news/easy/, which is part of NHK ONE. First you must tick the 'ご利用にあたって' terms box (no account needed, but NHK says households without a licence fee contract need one). The old JSON list https://www3.nhk.or.jp/news/easy/news-list.json now returns 401 'JWT token is required in the Authorization header'. The page is a Next.js app that gets articles from api.web.nhk with a token. The extension can only score articles after the user has accepted the terms in their own browser; the old JSON cannot be enumerated server-side.

items.title: WATANOC
items.titleEn: WATANOC: free web magazine in easy Japanese
items.creator: WATANOC
items.why: Short articles about Japan, each tagged N5-Beginner, N4-Pre-intermediate or N3-Intermediate, with furigana.
items.notes: WordPress site. RSS at https://watanoc.com/feed has JLPT-level categories (N5-Beginner etc.). The feed's newest items were dated 2016, so treat it as an archive. Articles are HTML.

items.title: ペッパー＆キャロット
items.creator: David Revoy
items.why: Short full-colour gag episodes with little dialogue per page; an open-licence comic you can read episode by episode.
items.notes: CC BY 4.0. The Japanese is a community translation, but it is the creator's official, credited one. Episodes: /ja/webcomic/ep01_Potion-of-Flight.html etc. Text is in the images (made from SVG sources in the project's repository), not HTML.

items.title: 青空文庫
items.creator: 青空文庫 volunteers
items.why: More than 17,000 public-domain Japanese works as plain HTML. Mostly older literary language, but it includes short children's stories.
items.notes: Enumerate: the full catalogue CSV is at https://www.aozora.gr.jp/index_pages/list_person_all_extended_utf8.zip (UTF-8, about 2 MB, verified). It has columns for work ID, title, kana spelling, author, and XHTML/text file URLs. Card pages are /cards/{personId}/card{workId}.html (UTF-8). Text pages are /cards/{personId}/files/{workId}_{fileId}.html, encoded Shift_JIS with ruby furigana markup. Many old texts use 旧字旧仮名, so filter on the 新字新仮名 column.

items.title: ごん狐
items.creator: 新美南吉
items.why: A short children's classic taught in every Japanese primary school; simple plot, but rural vocabulary and some older expressions.
items.notes: Very short (about 10 minutes for a native reader). Sad ending.

items.title: 手袋を買いに
items.creator: 新美南吉
items.why: A short, gentle children's story with lots of dialogue between a fox mother and her cub.

items.title: 注文の多い料理店
items.creator: 宮沢賢治
items.why: A short, funny and slightly creepy story built on repeated signs and instructions, which makes it easy to follow.

items.title: 蜘蛛の糸
items.creator: 芥川龍之介
items.why: A very short literary story (a few pages) with a simple parable structure; Buddhist and literary vocabulary.

items.title: 走れメロス
items.creator: 太宰治
items.why: A famous school text with a clear plot, but long sentences and old-fashioned dramatic narration.

items.title: 銀河鉄道の夜
items.creator: 宮沢賢治
items.why: A beloved novella, but dreamlike and full of poetic and scientific vocabulary.

items.title: 小説家になろう
items.creator: 株式会社ヒナプロジェクト
items.why: Over a million free web novels. Isekai/fantasy prose is repetitive and dialogue-heavy, so it is a common first step into native novels.
items.notes: Public JSON API, no key needed: https://api.syosetu.com/novelapi/api/?out=json&order=hyoka&lim=20&of=t-n-w-g-bg-l (fields: title, ncode, writer, genre, biggenre, length, end, general_all_no...). Filter with genre=/biggenre=, ncode=a-b-c, word=, length=. Rankings API: https://api.syosetu.com/rank/rankget/?out=json&rtype=YYYYMMDD-d|w|m|q (verified with rtype=20261101-m). Docs: https://dev.syosetu.com/man/api/ and https://dev.syosetu.com/man/rankapi/. Chapters are plain HTML at https://ncode.syosetu.com/{ncode}/{n}/. R18 works are on a separate API/host (noc), so exclude them.

items.title: 転生したらスライムだった件
items.titleEn: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
items.creator: 伏瀬
items.why: Easy-going first-person narration and game-like vocabulary that repeats a lot; many learners already know the anime.
items.notes: ncode N6316BN, 304 episodes on the web. The API reports end=0 (not marked complete). The web version differs from the published light novels.

items.title: 本好きの下剋上　～司書になるためには手段を選んでいられません～
items.creator: 香月美夜
items.why: Slice-of-life world-building with everyday vocabulary (food, family, crafts), but very long.
items.notes: ncode N4830BU, 677 episodes.

items.title: カクヨム
items.creator: KADOKAWA / はてな
items.why: KADOKAWA's free web-novel platform, like Narō but with more genres; chapters are HTML.
items.notes: No documented public API. Enumerate from the ranking pages (/rankings/{genre}/{daily|weekly|monthly}). Chapter pages are readable without login.

items.title: 少年ジャンプ＋
items.creator: 集英社
items.why: Shueisha's official manga app/site: first chapters and many ongoing series free to read, with furigana in most series.
items.notes: Series index at https://shonenjumpplus.com/series (links point to episode 1 at /episode/{id}). Pages are images, so the extension cannot score the text.

items.title: SPY×FAMILY
items.creator: 遠藤達哉
items.why: Popular family comedy with furigana, but spy jargon and fast banter put it at Natively L29; the first chapter is known to be hard.
items.notes: Some chapters free on Jump+; volumes sold by Shueisha.

items.title: ルリドラゴン
items.creator: 眞藤雅興
items.why: Low-key school slice of life with natural teen dialogue; Natively rates volume 3 at L23 (upper beginner to intermediate).

items.title: カドコミ (コミックウォーカー)
items.creator: KADOKAWA
items.why: KADOKAWA's free manga site; most series have free first episodes, including many light-novel and isekai adaptations.
items.notes: Series pages: /detail/{KC_xxxxxx_S}, with episodes under /detail/{series}/episodes/{episode}. The home page's JSON payload lists series codes. Pages are images. The site now brands itself 'カドコミ'.

items.title: よつばと！
items.creator: あずまきよひこ
items.why: The classic first manga for learners: a 5-year-old's everyday adventures, full furigana, Natively L18.
items.notes: Not legally free online. 16 volumes (as of 2025). Casual speech and some child-speech.

items.title: チーズスイートホーム
items.creator: こなみかなた
items.why: Short full-colour chapters about a kitten, very simple sentences and baby-talk; Natively rates the series L14, one of the easiest manga.

links.site: 講談社 公式えほん (2026)

items.notes: Chi's baby-talk (〜ちた etc.) is non-standard; warn beginners.

items.title: 魔女の宅急便
items.creator: 角野栄子
items.why: A children's novel learners pick as a first novel because of the Ghibli film; Natively L25, heavy on kana and onomatopoeia.
items.notes: 6 volumes (角川文庫 / 福音館 editions).

items.title: 窓ぎわのトットちゃん
items.titleEn: Totto-chan: The Little Girl at the Window
items.creator: 黒柳徹子
items.why: Short episodic chapters about a girl's school life; a learner reviewer called it mainly N3 grammar and a smooth read.
items.notes: Furigana edition exists (講談社青い鳥文庫).

items.title: Short Stories in Japanese for Intermediate Learners
items.titleEn: Short Stories in Japanese for Intermediate Learners
items.creator: Olly Richards (Teach Yourself)
items.why: Eight graded stories at CEFR B1-B2 with vocabulary lists, summaries and comprehension questions.
items.notes: ISBN 9781529377163 (2022). Audiobook also available. There is no Olly Richards Japanese 'beginners' book.

items.title: Learn Hiragana: The Ultimate Guide
items.creator: Tofugu
items.why: Picture mnemonics for every hiragana plus recall exercises, worksheets and a drill quiz; learners report finishing in a few hours to a week.
items.notes: step 1: hiragana. Free to read on the web (optional paid book with handwriting practice). Covers dakuten, combination kana, small tsu, pronunciation. Reading-first (no handwriting). English only.

items.title: Learn Katakana: The Ultimate Guide
items.creator: Tofugu
items.why: Same mnemonic method as the hiragana guide, for katakana.
items.notes: step 2: katakana, after hiragana. Free; English only. Tofugu YouTube: @tofugu (UC5elZt69ka5BM1r-XFeENbQ).

items.title: やさしい日本語
items.creator: NHK WORLD-JAPAN, supervised by the Japan Foundation
items.why: 48 ten-minute audio-drama lessons of everyday phrases, with free MP3 and PDF text, taught in the learner's own language.
items.notes: step 3: first phrases. Free for personal use (MP3 + PDF downloads). Offered in 18 languages on the web: Arabic, English, Russian, Urdu, Bengali, French, Korean, Spanish, Vietnamese, Burmese, Hindi, Persian, Swahili, Chinese, Indonesian, Portuguese, Thai, Turkish (only the English URL verified; other editions sit under the same lesson site). Best pick for learners whose native language isn't English.

items.title: いろどり 生活の日本語 入門
items.titleEn: Irodori: Japanese for Life in Japan - Starter (A1)
items.creator: The Japan Foundation
items.why: Official A1 coursebook (18 lessons) as PDF with MP3 audio, vocabulary lists and grammar worksheets, focused on practical survival tasks.
items.notes: step 4: structured A1 course. Free PDF download (site permits printing; sellers may only recover print cost). Levels: Starter A1, Elementary 1 A2, Elementary 2 A2, Pre-Intermediate A2/B1. Translated editions (Can-dos, instructions, vocabulary, grammar notes) in 20 languages: Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Mongolian, Indonesian, Khmer, Thai, Filipino, Vietnamese, Burmese, Nepali, Portuguese, Spanish, Ukrainian, Russian, Uzbek, French, Lao, Bengali, Hindi - see https://www.irodori.jpf.go.jp/en/editions.html. Do kana (steps 1-2) first.

items.title: JF日本語eラーニング みなと
items.creator: The Japan Foundation
items.why: Japan Foundation's platform of self-study and tutor-supported online courses, including many free A1 courses (kana, Marugoto A1) explained in different languages.
items.notes: step 4 alternative: guided A1 online course. Account required. Each course tagged Free or Charged; many A1 self-study courses are free. Site menu: English, Japanese, Spanish, Chinese, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese; course explanations also in French, German, Hungarian, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic.

items.title: エリンが挑戦！にほんごできます。
items.titleEn: Erin's Challenge! I Can Speak Japanese
items.creator: The Japan Foundation
items.why: 25 short video skits following a student in Japan, each built around one situation (greetings, asking directions) with key phrases and culture quizzes.
items.notes: step 3: listening/phrases with video. Watch online on the site (no login seen); site interface Japanese and English (/en/). Subtitle languages not confirmed on the page. Companion app and YouTube playlist linked from the site.

items.title: にほんご多読ブックス 無料の読みもの
items.creator: NPO Tadoku Supporters (tadoku.org)
items.why: Free graded readers from Level Start (picture books) to Level 5, with furigana, hiragana-only versions and audio narration - the first real reading after kana.

text.license: free to read online; PDFs downloadable/printable for personal use (no formal licence stated)

items.notes: step 5: first reading (Level Start/0 right after kana). Page interface Japanese/English. Some titles have YouTube narration.

items.title: Duolingo Japanese
items.creator: Duolingo
items.why: Gamified bite-size lessons including kana drills; fine as a daily habit next to a real course.
items.notes: any step: daily habit. Free app/web, optional subscription. Verified URL is the English-speaker course; Japanese is also offered from some other base languages (check app). LingoDeer (https://www.lingodeer.com/, freemium, 16-language site menu) is a grammar-stronger alternative.
